title: Protocol for wireless deep brain stimulation in freely behaving mice with infrared light
protocol: Take out the aliquoted AAV from the −80°C freezer.
Thaw the virus on ice.
Sterilize all surgical tools with an autoclave.
Put the sterilized tools on a sterile gauze pad.
Weigh and anesthetize a mouse with intraperitoneal injection of ketamine (80 mg/kg) and dexdomitor (1 mg/kg) cocktail.
Put the mouse on a heating pad of a homeothermic monitoring system with the temperature set to 37°C to prevent hypothermia.
Verify the degree of anesthesia through toe pinch before starting the surgery.
Apply vet ointment on both eyes of the mouse to keep them moist throughout the surgery.
Subcutaneously inject buprenorphine SR (1 mg/kg) for analgesia.
Subcutaneously inject 0.2 ml of prewarmed saline to prevent dehydration.
Remove the hair using the hair removal lotion.
Use an alcohol pad to gently moisturize the hair, then apply the hair removal lotion using a cotton-tipped applicator.
Remove the lotion with a clean cotton-tipped applicator after 1-2 minutes.
Sterilize the exposed skin with betadine and 70% ethanol, alternating three times.
Thoroughly depilate the head and neck of the mouse.
Fix the animal in the stereotaxic frame.
Fix the left ear bar, and gently move the mouse head forward so that the ear canal is close to the ear bar.
Hold the mouse head still, then gradually put the right ear bar in place.
Check if no lateral movement of the head is possible.
Pull down the lower jaw with forceps and insert the maxillary incisors into the opening of the adapter.
Press gently on the head with a cotton-tipped applicator to check for appropriate fixing.
Make a 1-mm incision on the scalp using a sterile scalpel.
Gradually elongate the incision to expose the skull using sterilized spring scissors.
Ensure that both bregma and lambda are exposed on the skull.
Adjust the angle of the head to make it horizontal.
Measure the DV positions of bregma and lambda on the skull with a blunt needle.
Adjust the angle of the head so that bregma and lambda have the same DV positions.
Mark the position of VTA on the skull using a sterilized pencil.
Gently drill a hole with a diameter of 0.5 mm on the marked position on the skull.
Use a stereoscopic microscope to visualize and control the drilling process.
Load approximately 3 μL of AAV solution into the Hamilton syringe.
Fix the Hamilton syringe onto the stereotaxic frame.
Place the tip of the syringe at the bregma and zero the positioning system.
Raise the syringe by 5 mm, then move it to AP: -3.5 mm, ML: 0.4 mm.
Lower the heel of bevel of the needle to the DV location of VTA (-4.2 mm).
Ensure the heel of bevel of the needle is positioned at the correct depth for precise viral transduction.
Wait for 5 min after advancing the needle to the target.
Inject 2.5 μL of AAV solution at a rate of 0.1 μL/min.
Wait for 2 min before withdrawing the needle.
Put the incised scalp back in place to cover the exposed skull.
Apply Vetbond tissue adhesive to seal the skin.
Apply antibiotic ointment around the wound with a cotton-tipped applicator.
Subcutaneously inject atipamezole (1 mg/kg) to help accelerate recovery.
Place the mouse back into its cage, with half of the cage on top of a heating pad set to 37°C.
Ensure the burr hole is accessible and large enough for needle insertion.
Enlarge the burr hole using a drill if necessary.
Use a stereoscopic microscope for better visualization during drilling.
Load approximately 3 μL of MINDS solution (1.8 mg/mL) into the syringe.
Inject 2.5 μL of MINDS solution into the VTA as described in steps 15–22.
For control experiments, inject 1× HHBS instead of MINDS.
Prepare the Y-maze for conditioned place preference testing.
Cover the bottom of the Y-maze with mouse cage bedding.
Ensure that the thickness of the bedding is similar to a regular housing cage.
Print black grating patterns on white paper with a 5-mm grating width and a 1-cm center-to-center interval between neighboring gratings.
Print the grating patterns in both horizontal and vertical directions.
Tape the horizontal and vertical grating patterns on the wall of two arm terminals of the Y maze.
For the third arm terminal, tape blank white paper on the wall.
Set up a video camera over the Y maze with sufficient field of view covering the entire Y maze.
Set air conditioning to maintain a stable ambient temperature at 25°C.
Run a 30-min pretest on Day1.
Place the mouse in the central triangle of the Y maze.
Turn on the video camera to record the trajectory and behavior of the mouse.
Remove the three doors that separate the central triangle and the three arms simultaneously.
Let the mouse freely explore the entire Y maze for 30 min.
After the pretest is finished, remove the mouse from the Y maze.
Put the mouse back to its home cage.
Clean the Y maze with Virkon-S followed by 70% ethanol between animals.
Connect a fiber collimator to the 1,064-nm laser output fiber on Day2 to Day4.
Adjust the distance between the collimator and the targeted arm terminal of the Y maze to be ∼ 1 m for a circular laser spot with a diameter of 1 cm.
Fix the fiber collimator on a locking ball and socket mount.
Ensure that the angle of the collimator can freely adjust to cover a 5 cm × 5 cm area at the end of the targeted arm terminal.
Set up the function generator to output a high voltage pulse train with 20 Hz repetition rate and 30% duty cycle.
Connect the function generator's output to the laser control box trigger input via a BNC cable.
Turn on the laser and monitor its output power using a power meter.
Adjust the temporal average output power density of the laser spot to 10 mW/mm².
Set up a thermal camera to monitor the mouse temperature in the targeted arm terminal of the Y maze.
Place the mouse inside the Y maze, turn on the video camera, and remove the three doors.
Aim the laser beam at the mouse's head when it enters the 5 cm × 5 cm area at the end of the targeted arm terminal.
Temporarily turn off the laser if the mouse's head tilts, preventing accurate aiming, until the head returns to its horizontal position.
Monitor the temperature on the mouse head through the thermal camera continuously.
Turn down the laser output to 0 whenever the scalp temperature exceeds 39°C.
Resume laser output at 10 mW/mm² when the scalp temperature drops below 38°C.
Turn off the laser when the mouse leaves the targeted arm terminal area.
Wear appropriate laser safety goggles when working with lasers.
Avoid aiming the laser beam on the fur of the mouse.
Perform a 30-min posttest identical to the pretest procedures on Day5.
Conduct comprehensive control experiments involving mice without TRPV1 transduction and MINDS injection.
Compare place preference behavior between the pretest and posttest as an internal control for NIR-II light.
Deeply anesthetize the mouse with intraperitoneal injection of ketamine (120 mg/kg) and dexdomitor (1 mg/kg).
Euthanize the mouse through sequential transcardial perfusion of 12-mL 1× PBS and 24-mL 4% PFA.
Dissect the brain from the skull and immerse it in 15-mL of 4% PFA at 4°C for 24 h.
Remove the brain from 4% PFA.
Cut a 3–5 mm thick coronal tissue block including VTA using a brain slicer.
Immerse the brain tissue block into 10-mL of 30% sucrose solution and keep it at 4°C overnight (12–20 h).
Fill a cryomold with O.C.T. compound and transfer the brain tissue block into it.
Wait for 30 min while preparing dry ice/methanol slurry in a 10 cm petri-dish.
Place the petri-dish on top of a foam box cap to keep the temperature low.
Add more dry ice if needed until the system equilibrates.
Wear thermally-insulated gloves when working with dry ice.
Transfer the brain into a new cryomold filled with O.C.T. compound.
Remove any air bubbles surrounding the brain tissue with blunt tweezers.
Freeze-embed the brain tissue.
Grasp the mold with long forceps and gently place it into the dry ice/methanol slurry.
Ensure methanol does not contact the O.C.T. compound or tissue directly.
Wait until the O.C.T. compound freezes and turns white, starting from the bottom up and from the sides to the center within 1–2 min.
Transfer the mold onto dry ice after the O.C.T. compound fully turns white.
Obtain 20-μm brain sections using a cryostat.
Put the O.C.T.-embedded brain tissue inside the chamber of the cryostat and wait until it equilibrates at −20°C.
Mount the tissue block onto a sample holder using a thin layer of O.C.T. compound.
Adjust the angle of the tissue block and the anti-rolling plate to obtain a flat section.
Trim extra tissue until VTA is exposed.
Cut 20-μm sections and transfer them to ice-cold 1× PBS solution using a small brush.
Store brain sections at 4°C for up to 1 day.
Rinse brain sections 3 times in 1× PBS for 10 min each on a shaker at 450 rpm and 4°C.
Prepare the blocking solution by adding 5% normal goat/donkey serum and 0.3% Triton X-100 in 1× PBS.
Place brain sections in the blocking solution for 1 h at room temperature (20°C–25°C) on a shaker at 150 rpm.
Use serum from the same species as the secondary antibody to make the blocking solution.
Incubate brain sections with AffiniPure Fab Fragment Goat Anti-Mouse IgG (H+L) at a dilution ratio of 1:65 in 1× PBS for 1 h at room temperature on a shaker at 150 rpm.
Rinse the brain sections three times in 1× PBS for 10 min each on a shaker at 450 rpm and 4°C.
Transfer the brain sections from the blocking solution to the primary antibody solution after blocking finishes.
Incubate the brain sections overnight (12–20 h) at 4°C on a shaker at 150 rpm.
Rinse the brain sections three times in 1× PBS with 0.05% Triton X-100 for 10 min each on a shaker at 450 rpm and 4°C.
Prepare the fluorescent secondary antibody solution by diluting antibodies with appropriate dilution ratios in 1× PBS supplemented with 5% normal goat/donkey serum and 0.1% Triton X-100.
Transfer the brain sections from the rinsing solution in step 44 to the secondary antibody solution.
Incubate the brain sections for 1.5 h at room temperature (20°C–25°C) on a shaker at 150 rpm.
Rinse the brain sections 3 times in 1× PBS for 10 min each on a shaker at 450 rpm and 4°C.
Mount the brain sections onto glass slides.
Add a few droplets of 1× PBS on a Superfrost Plus glass slide.
Gently pick up a brain section and transfer it to the PBS droplet on the glass slide.
Use Kimwipes to dry the PBS, ensuring there are no wrinkles or folds in the brain section.
Mount up to 2 brain sections per glass slide.
Add 4–5 μL of Prolong Gold Antifade Mountant to the brain section and mount a coverslip on top by slowly lowering the coverslip to touch the mounting solution.
Use clear nail polish to seal the edges of the coverslip to prevent the brain section from drying.
Allow the nail polish to dry in dark and keep the slides horizontal at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 24 h.
Store the slides in a light-tight container wrapped with aluminum foil before imaging.
Perform fluorescence imaging of the brain sections using a confocal microscope.
